# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — first capability from empty seed: no-formula value contract + inspect/reconcile/verify procedure
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md "How your result is judged" (cluster A, about 13 tasks): formulas read back None under data_only with no recalc, so compute in Python and write literals even when the user asks for a formula, VBA or macro. Use real types and never write error text.
  - prompt.md Procedure steps 1–3 (cluster B): inspect the target region, examples and fills. Derive the rule from the sheet and check that it reproduces the pre-filled examples. Evaluate per row.
  - prompt.md step 4 + notes (cluster C): targeted openpyxl write instead of pandas `to_excel`. Fill the whole range, including a header row for mirrored blocks. xlsxwriter is absent. Copy the exact output_path.
  - prompt.md steps 5–6 + task_template.md (cluster D): new user template drops "once that file exists, you are done". It adds inspect → write literals → reload with data_only and print → finish with a no-code reply.
- Expected effect + safety: should fix most of cluster A (37378, 46897, 6698, 7902, 8942, 55049, 53383, 9569, 55979, 37456, 54144, 53647, 56563) plus some of B/C (39046, 48527, 227-40, 80-42, 51-12). Passing tasks already write literals and mostly finish with prose, so the rules codify their behavior.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: B semantics (43436 month-end-open counting, 50768 matrix orientation, 267-18 fill detection). 59196 is undiagnosed.
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT broke/fixed. If cluster A remains, add a worked example of a formula request turned into a computed literal. If B remains, add a worked example of reconciling the rule with pre-filled examples. If any passing task broke, check whether it is round budget (a longer inspection) or the openpyxl-vs-pandas preference.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.825 Δ=+0.375 · fixed={227-40, 37378, 37456, 39046, 46897, 48527, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={2768} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.825 Δ=+0.375 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 (2/3)
- Hypothesis: the remaining 7 failures are not semantics-only. 4 share a turn-protocol fault: fabricated "Output:" text, and real stdout treated as user feedback or resubmitted unchanged. 5 share layout/mechanics faults: header row offset, column index, matrix axes, cached formula values lost on save, blank rows, float threshold.
- Edits: task_template turn contract + debug-on-mismatch step. prompt.md: row-numbered inspection, preview offset/"Unnamed", axis labels, point-in-time headers, columns by header name, plus 3 practical notes (blank rows/max_row, cached formula loss, float tolerance).
- Expected fixes: 51-12, 59196, 267-18, 80-42, 2768, 43436, 50768. Risk: a longer prompt might lengthen the inspection rounds. All additions are conditional or inspection-only.
- What to try next iteration: if a task still fails, compare its trace with these exact notes. If the note was read but ignored, use a worked example. If a passing task broke, consider removing the debug-step wording first.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.875 Δ=+0.050 · fixed={267-18, 51-12, 59196, 80-42} · broke={37456, 48527} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

- VERIFIED (cand_0001, +0.375): stating that the grader reads `data_only=True` without recalc, so values must be written as literals and never as formulas, plus a reload-and-verify step, fixed 16 tasks.
- VERIFIED by simulation (cand_0002 diagnosis): openpyxl save drops cached formula values inside the answer range (267-18). `ws.max_row` overcounts because of blank rows (80-42). Float `>=` thresholds need an epsilon (51-12). The preview's "Unnamed" headers mean the header is not in Excel row 1 (59196). Column mapping by position read the answer column (2768).

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: diagnosed all 22 failing traces against the golden cells before writing anything. This showed that the dominant failure (about 13 of 22) is a grader-contract mismatch (formula strings with no recalc), not reasoning. So the first edit is a CONTRACT plus a procedure, delivered in both the system prompt and the editable task_template, since the old template's "once that file exists, you are done" line suppressed verification.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next iteration: use RESULT broke/fixed to separate contract wins from semantics failures. For the remaining semantics cluster, switch lever to a compact worked example rather than more rules. Watch the round count: a longer procedure might push slow tasks past 30 rounds.

- (cand_0002) Re-running the agent's own approach with only the root cause fixed, then scoring it against the golden with the grader's transform rules, separated "right idea, mechanical bug" (5/7 tasks) from true semantic misreads. This was much more informative than reading the feedback text. Also scan passing traces for the same anomaly (fabricated output appeared in 8 passing runs) before judging the blast radius.

files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration cand_0002 (2/3), starting from the champion cand_0001 (val 0.825, 33/40). I diagnosed all 7 failing traces against their `*_golden.xlsx` answer cells. Every rollout had `error: None`, so there were no infra faults. For 5 tasks I re-ran a corrected version of the agent's own approach and scored it with the same transform_value rules: 80-42, 267-18, 51-12, 43436 and 2768 all PASS once the root cause is fixed. For 50768 and 59196 I verified by reading the gold cells against the sheet's labels and header row.

## Ranked issue list
| rank | cluster | tasks | root cause (verified) | tag | file chosen |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | X. Fabricated output / exec result misread as user feedback / identical resubmits | 51-12, 43436, 59196, 50768 (also present in passing runs) | The agent writes a predicted "Output:" after its code, then treats the real stdout as "user feedback" or "another dataset". It bends its rule to fit (51-12) or resubmits the same code for 11 rounds (59196). | STRUCTURE (interaction contract) | task_template.md (it governs the turn protocol) |
| 2 | Y. Sheet layout misread: header row / column index / axes | 59196 (header in row 2, preview "Unnamed"), 2768 (columns off by one, so it read the answer column as qty), 50768 (matrix axes swapped) | Positions assumed instead of read from labels. The preview is offset by one row. | KNOWLEDGE + PROCEDURE | prompt.md step 1–3 |
| 3 | Z. openpyxl/Python mechanics | 267-18 (cached formula values lost on save, so G1=None), 80-42 (blank rows copied, max_row overcounts), 51-12 (`110 >= 100*1.1` False) | Environment facts the model doesn't apply by default | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule + reason) | prompt.md Practical notes |
| 4 | W. Point-in-time semantics | 43436 ("Open by end of May" = created ≤ EOM and not closed by EOM) | Loose prose preferred over the header's precise meaning | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md step 2 |

## Edits (lever, verify, blast radius)
1. **task_template.md: turn contract** (lever: CONTRACT + soften the step-3 failure path into an ordered debug step). End the reply after the code block. The next message is real stdout from the sandbox, not the user, and never reveals the answer. Don't predict output. On a mismatch, print the inputs and intermediates rather than changing the rule to match the printout.
   - Verify: 51-12 trace (it rationalises "B6 value: 2" as user feedback), 43436 (it calls the real output "values from a different dataset"), 59196 (identical code resubmitted while writing None).
   - Blast radius: every task. Passing runs that already wait for output are unaffected. Passing runs with fabricated blocks (227-40, 31628, 45635, 46897, 48620, 53383, 59595, 9569) reached the right answer anyway, and the edit only stops the hallucinated text. Risk is low because no new work is demanded.
2. **prompt.md step 1: print with Excel row numbers, preview offset, "Unnamed" headers, look at the row above / column left of the range** (lever: PROCEDURE + KNOWLEDGE).
   - Verify: 59196 read headers from empty row 1. 50768 never printed E12:E14 / F15:H15.
   - Blast radius: inspection only. Every passing task already does step-1 inspection, so this adds one print pattern.
3. **prompt.md step 2: matrix axes from labels; point-in-time headers** (lever: missing rule with reason).
   - Verify: 50768 gold H12="4, 6" needs Impact on the rows. A 43436 simulation of the snapshot rule PASSES.
   - Blast radius: conditional on a matrix or an "as of / by end of" header. In the passing set, only 382-10 and 395-36 are grid-like, and both already read their labels.
4. **prompt.md step 3: columns by header text, never read the answer column as input, print one parsed record** (lever: PROCEDURE).
   - Verify: 2768 `row[7]` = "Expected outcome" used as qty. The row-order allocation simulation PASSES.
   - Blast radius: all computing tasks. It's a debugging print plus a lookup idiom, with no semantic change for correctly mapped tasks.
5. **prompt.md notes: blank rows / max_row** (lever: missing rule with reason).
   - Verify: 80-42 Henry max_row 2000 vs 999 data rows. The skip-blank simulation PASSES.
   - Blast radius: copy/consolidate/count tasks (e.g. 47798, 48588 dedup/filter copies). Skipping all-None rows doesn't change outputs that have no blank rows.
6. **prompt.md notes: cached formula values lost on save** (lever: KNOWLEDGE).
   - Verify: 267-18 G1 read back as None. The simulation that writes cached literals PASSES.
   - Blast radius: only answer ranges that contain existing formula cells.
7. **prompt.md notes: float tolerance** (lever: KNOWLEDGE + minimal example).
   - Verify: 51-12. The epsilon simulation gives 4, which equals gold.
   - Blast radius: threshold/equality comparisons on computed floats. The epsilon is 1e-9, far below the grader's 2-dp rounding.

## Skipped
- ARGB fill note (267-18 first checked `'FFFF00'` but recovered by itself; the gold-relevant failure was the cached-value loss).
- A worked example per cluster, to keep the prompt short for the frontier reader.
- Any task-specific values.

## Placeholders
I validated `task_template.md` after stripping the comment: Formatter fields = {instruction, spreadsheet_path, spreadsheet_content, instruction_type, answer_position, output_path, max_turns}, and `.format()` succeeds. `prompt.md` is not `.format()`ed by the adapter (line 1378), so its literal braces are safe.

## Subagents
None. Work was serial, per the session's tool policy.

"""SpreadsheetBench adapter template — optimize a spreadsheet agent's system prompt.

Ready-to-use cap-evolve adapter for SpreadsheetBench
(https://github.com/RUCKBReasoning/SpreadsheetBench). Supports ANY litellm-compatible
provider — configure via env vars (see model_config.py).

SETUP:
  1. Get the harness code (Docker/Jupyter sandbox + prompt/scoring helpers). cap-evolve
     vendors it as a filtered git subtree at third_party/spreadsheetbench — point at that,
     or clone+filter upstream yourself (see third_party/spreadsheetbench/NOTICE.md):
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_HARNESS_DIR=/path/to/cap-evolve/third_party/spreadsheetbench

  2. Fetch the dataset (NOT vendored — tens of MB of xlsx files, fetched at run time):
       ci/benchmarks/spreadsheetbench/fetch_data.sh /some/cache/dir
     then point at the extracted folder (contains dataset.json + spreadsheet/):
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_DATA_DIR=/some/cache/dir/sample_data_200
     SPREADSHEETBENCH_VARIANT selects which release: `sample_200`, `full_912` (the original
     912-task set, 3 graded copies per task) or `verified_400` (the 400-task verified
     re-release, 1 graded copy per task — what recent published work evaluates on). The
     adapter reads the number of graded copies off disk, so all three just work.

  3. Install Docker (required — each task runs in its own sandboxed container) and,
     for accurate scoring of formula-bearing outputs, LibreOffice:
       sudo apt install libreoffice-calc   # Debian/Ubuntu
       sudo dnf install libreoffice-calc   # RHEL/Fedora
       brew install --cask libreoffice     # macOS
     Scoring degrades gracefully (skips recalculation) if LibreOffice is absent — but
     silently: a formula-only cell then reads as empty and never matches, so a task the
     agent actually solved scores 0. Treat the "LibreOffice not found" warning as a
     setup error, not a nicety. Upstream's docstring asks for 7.5+; RHEL 9's 7.1.8.1
     recalculates correctly through `--convert-to xlsx` and is verified in use.

  4. Install adapter deps: pip install pandas openpyxl docker tornado requests

  5. Copy this directory to .capevolve/project/adapters/, copy model_config.py alongside.

  6. Set env vars (in .env or shell) — any litellm provider, see model_config.py:
       MODEL=gpt-4.1-mini  OPENAI_API_KEY=«redacted»       # OpenAI
       MODEL=anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=«redacted»  # Anthropic
       MODEL=litellm_proxy/my-model  LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE=http://proxy:4000  LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY=«redacted»

  7. Optional env vars:
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_TASK_IDS=59196,58568         # comma-separated subset (default: all 200)
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_MAX_TURNS=5                  # rounds of code-exec interaction per task
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_ROWS=5                       # preview rows shown per sheet in the prompt
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_CONCURRENCY=4                # parallel tasks (each = one Docker container)
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_EXEC_TIMEOUT=180             # per code-exec call timeout (s)
       SPREADSHEETBENCH_LIBREOFFICE_BIN=/path/to/soffice

  8. Run: cap-evolve check && cap-evolve run

WHAT THIS OPTIMIZES — ALL the text the agent reads, in two files:
  - prompt.md         the system prompt: who the agent is, how it should work.
  - task_template.md  the per-task user message: how the job is framed, what the fields
                      mean, and the interaction contract. Optional — no file falls back to
                      the built-in _TASK_TEMPLATE, so older capabilities are unaffected.
  Keeping the job description frozen in this file used to leave ~60% of the agent's
  instruction surface un-optimizable, including the line "once that file exists, you are
  done" — which encourages exactly the dominant failure (a wrong-but-present output file).
  Per-task VALUES (instruction, paths, preview, answer_position) are still supplied by the
  adapter through placeholders that live() validates; see _task_template_error.
